Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

mcqs.q: What does Labov's research show about language variation?
options: Labov showed that working-class people speak ungrammatically.
Overt prestige is loud speech and covert prestige is quiet speech.
Labov showed that everyone speaks the same way regardless of background.
Language varies systematically by social class, gender, age and context — and speakers shift style depending on formality, often unconsciously.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between descriptive and prescriptive approaches to language?
options: Descriptivists describe how language is actually used; prescriptivists rule on how language ought to be used — modern linguistics is descriptivist.
Labov showed that everyone speaks the same way regardless of background.
Both terms mean the same — analysing language scientifically.
Descriptivists describe written language and prescriptivists describe spoken language.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between overt and covert prestige?
options: Only standard language has prestige; non-standard varieties have none.

Overt prestige is the high status of standard varieties recognised by society (RP, Standard English); covert prestige is the hidden status of non-standard varieties within particular groups, signalling solidarity or toughness.
Overt prestige is loud speech and covert prestige is quiet speech.
Both terms mean the same — analysing language scientifically.
